summary.title: Client-Side Architecture Basics [Guide]
summary.one_liner: A guide to applying general software design principles to client-side web apps, with React as the main example, covering the separate layers of concern from view to state management to app logic.
keywords: how to structure a react app
takeaways: Client-side apps benefit from upfront architecture design, separating discrete layers of concern.
The principles (robustness, flexibility, testability, maintainability) transfer across view-layer libraries and frameworks, not only React.
Tools such as state management libraries and API/transport layers each suit particular problems; choose them deliberately.
The guide covers the view layer, the different forms of state management, and how to handle interaction (app) logic.
summary.summary: The author describes frustration with constantly changing React best practices and proposes returning to first principles of software design for client-side apps. The guide sets out architectural standards for web front ends, focusing on React while noting the ideas apply to any view layer. It walks through the layers of concern in a client-side app, from the view layer through state management to interaction logic. Prerequisites are familiarity with a view library or framework and at least one state management approach. The page mentions modern tools such as React, xState, and Apollo Client in its description.
